claim: Intraday returns of Chinese equities exhibit predictable patterns at the half‑hour level, with significant momentum and reversal effects within a trading day.
universe: Chinese A‑share market (Shanghai Composite Index, Shenzhen Component Index, CSI 300) intraday data from 2019‑01‑02 to 2021‑09‑01

horizon.reason: the paper studies half‑hour predictability within the same trading day rather than a multi‑day forecasting horizon

signal_construction.value: univariate linear regression on half‑hour returns, later refined with additional explanatory variables (overnight return, dummy for Monday/Friday)

reported_results.name: first_half_day_to_second_half_day_coeff
reported_results.quoted: the regression coefficient is 0.1294, which means that the first-half-day rate of return has a positive impact on the second-half-day rate of return.

reported_results.name: previous_day_full_day_to_second_half_day_coeff
reported_results.quoted: the regression coefficient is -0.0534, which means that the daily rate of return of the previous day has a similar effect on the rate of return of the second half of the next day.

reported_results.name: first_half_hour_to_fifth_hour_coeff
reported_results.note: coefficient for first half‑hour return predicting the fifth half‑hour return (Table 3)

what_is_missing: the provided passages do not contain quantitative estimates of transaction costs nor net excess returns after accounting for those costs, limiting assessment of economic profitability

source.title: Exploring the Predictability of Intraday Returns

transposability.what_transfers: half‑hour return momentum patterns; positive regression coefficients between early and later half‑hours; reversal effects between first half‑hour and later periods
what_does_not_transfer: definition of overnight return based on Chinese market closing/opening prices
transaction‑cost environment unique to Chinese equities
transposability.what_aligns_well: the identified intraday momentum between early and later half‑hours mirrors similar patterns observed in high‑frequency futures markets
